summary: Tested the new GDPR account-deletion endpoint DELETE /api/account/me end-to-end. 8/8 pytest tests passed against the public preview URL. Verified auth failures (missing/malformed/invalid Bearer all return 401), happy-path deletion returns 200 with correct response shape (status, message, deleted_counts, user_doc_existed=true), all 10 user-owned collections appear in deleted_counts, seeded product/sale/expense are actually purged (counts >=1), users-row deleted exactly once (counts.users == 1), ambassador collections are NOT touched (not present in counts), idempotent 2nd call returns 200 with user_doc_existed=false and empty/zero deleted_counts. Note: after deletion GET /api/auth/profile returns 404 (not 401) because data_api.get_current_user only validates JWT signature, not user existence — the spec explicitly allows either status, so this is acceptable.

minor.issue: Uses deprecated datetime.utcnow() in the audit log (account_api.py:105). Works on Python 3.11 (the runtime) but emits a DeprecationWarning on 3.12+. Cosmetic only.

account_api.py creates its own AsyncIOMotorClient (account_api.py:46) separate from data_api/server clients — three connection pools to the same DB. Matches existing project convention but inefficient. No functional impact.

After account is purged, profile endpoint returns 404 'Utilisateur non trouvé' instead of 401. Spec allows either; flag only if you prefer the 401 behaviour — would require reading users in get_current_user.

action_items: Optional: consider migrating datetime.utcnow() -> datetime.now(timezone.utc) in account_api.py:105 for future-proofing.

Optional: if you want post-deletion API calls to return 401 (not 404), have get_current_user verify the user still exists in db.users (would also force token invalidation server-side on account purge).
No blocking issues — endpoint behaves exactly as the GDPR spec requires.
critical_code_review_comments: account_api.py is small (~140 lines), well-commented, and properly excludes ambassador collections per requirement.
Error handling per-collection (deleted_counts[col] = -1 on exception, continues purge) is the right call for right-to-be-forgotten — partial purge is better than aborting.
Audit log is anonymized correctly (only last-4 of phone), good GDPR practice.
USER_OWNED_COLLECTIONS tuple matches the spec exactly (10 collections).
seed_data_creation: Each happy-path test class spins up a fresh user via /api/auth/phone-login with a unique +243* phone (timestamp suffix). One product + one sale + one expense are seeded and immediately purged by the test. No residue left in DB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_account_deletion.py. Run with: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=<public_url> pytest backend/tests/test_account_deletion.py -v. Tests use unique phone numbers per run so they're safe to re-run. Note that data_api's brute-force middleware on /auth/phone-login (5 attempts / 5 min per IP) means heavy parallel test runs from the same IP may hit 429 — the test calls pytest.skip() on 429.
rca_of_issue: No bugs found. The endpoint implementation matches the GDPR specification.
